=== PMID: 27501892 ===

Title: Decrease of pulmonary blood flow detected by phase contrast MRI is correlated with a decrease in lung volume and increase of lung fibrosis area determined by computed tomography in interstitial lung disease.

Journal/Date: European journal of radiology (2016)

MeSH Keywords: Adult, Aged, Contrast Media, Female, Hemodynamics, Humans, Image Enhancement, Lung


--- ABSTRACT ---
[PURPOSE]: Lung volume and pulmonary blood flow decrease in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD). The purpose of this study was to assess the relationship between pulmonary blood flow and lung volume in ILD patients.
[METHODS]: This research was approved by the institutional review board. Twenty-seven patients (9 men, 18 women; mean age, 59 years; range, 24-79 years) with ILD were included. Blood flow was assessed in the pulmonary trunk and the left and right pulmonary arteries by phase contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Lung volume and the computed tomography (CT) visual score that indicates the severity of ILD were assessed on the left and right sides by thin-section CT scanning. Lung volume was automatically measured by lung analysis software (VINCENT Ver. 4). The CT visual score was measured by averaging the proportion of abnormal lung area at five anatomic levels. Pearson's correlation coefficient was used to determine the relationship between pulmonary blood flow and lung volume.
[RESULTS]: Pulmonary blood flow showed a significant correlation with lung volume (both: r=0.52, p=0.006; left: r=0.61, p=0.001; right: r=0.54, p=0.004) and CT visual score (both: r=-0.39, p=0.04; left: r=-0.48, p=0.01; right: r=-0.38, p=0.04). Partial correlation analysis, controlled for age, height and weight, showed a significant correlation between pulmonary blood flow and lung volume (both: r=0.43, p=0.03; left: r=0.55, p=0.005; right: r=0.48, p=0.01) and CT visual score (both: r=-0.58, p=0.003; left: r=-0.51, p=0.01; right: r=-0.64, p=0.001).
[CONCLUSION]: In ILD, reduced pulmonary blood flow is associated with reduced lung volume and increased abnormal lung area.

Title: Estimation of pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary fibrosis by phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging.

Journal/Date: Japanese journal of radiology (2011)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[PURPOSE]: The aim of this study was to assess pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) in patients with pulmonary fibrosis (PF) by phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
[MATERIALS AND METHODS]: Subjects were 11 healthy volunteers and 11 patients with PF. Using phase-contrast MRI, we measured pulmonary arterial blood flow and calculated the parameters of PVR. Parameters were compared between volunteers and patients using unpaired t-tests. The diagnostic capability of the parameters was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Patients underwent respiratory function tests (RFTs) and chest computed tomography (CT), and they were correlated with MRI parameters.
[RESULTS]: Most MRI parameters were significantly different between volunteers and patients (t-test P values were <0.05 in 9 of 10 parameters). [CONCLUSION]: Our findings suggest that PVR derived from phase-contrast MRI is significantly higher in patients with PF than in volunteers. However, all but two of these parameters may not correlate with the severity of PF.

key_findings.finding: Direct human evidence was identified in one paired-measurement study (PMID 27501892; 27 patients with ILD): pulmonary blood flow measured in the pulmonary trunk and right/left pulmonary arteries by phase-contrast MRI correlated positively with CT-derived lung volume (both lungs r=0.52, p=0.006; left r=0.61, p=0.001; right r=0.54, p=0.004). Thus, lower flow was associated with lower lung volume. Associations remained significant after adjustment for age, height, and weight (both r=0.43, p=0.03; left r=0.55, p=0.005; right r=0.48, p=0.01).

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract with paired methods and correlation statistics

key_findings.finding: The same direct study found an inverse association between pulmonary blood flow and CT visual score representing abnormal/fibrotic lung area: both lungs r=-0.39, p=0.04; left r=-0.48, p=0.01; right r=-0.38, p=0.04. Adjusted partial correlations were also inverse and significant (both r=-0.58, p=0.003; left r=-0.51, p=0.01; right r=-0.64, p=0.001). Therefore, lower flow was associated with greater CT-abnormal/fibrosis area.

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract with CT visual-score definition and unadjusted/adjusted statistics

key_findings.finding: The ILD subtype was not specified in the available abstract for the 2016 paired study; PubTator annotations classify it broadly as interstitial lung disease/fibrosis in humans. The CT method was thin-section CT with visual scoring based on the average proportion of abnormal lung at five anatomic levels, and automated lung-volume analysis used VINCENT Ver. 4.

A related human study in pulmonary fibrosis (PMID 21927998; 11 patients plus 11 controls) measured pulmonary arterial flow by phase-contrast MRI and CT visual score, reporting an inverse correlation between CT visual score and average flow volume (r=-0.60, p=0.031). However, it did not report paired CT-derived lung volume, so it is direct evidence for the flow–CT severity direction but not for the full flow–lung-volume/fibrosis-area pairing requested.

The available evidence supports the proposed correlation direction, but is not sufficient to generalize across ILD subtypes: the key direct study pooled 27 ILD patients without specifying subtype in the abstract. Other retrieved studies involving idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis used different perfusion MRI approaches or did not perform the requested paired phase-contrast-flow plus CT lung-volume/fibrosis analysis, so they are mechanistic/indirect rather than confirmatory direct evidence.
